title: Why Don't Tower Cranes Fall Over?
description:
A tower crane is a thin steel pole, sometimes taller than a thirty story building, with a long arm sticking out to one side. It lifts tonnes of steel over the heads of people, and on a windy night, nobody is in it. By every instinct, it should fall over. It almost never does. Today, eleven parts of a tower crane, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 11 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:04 1. The concrete blocks on the short arm
2:18 2. The hook that lifts less at the tip
3:29 3. The hidden foundation
4:39 4. The mast that grows
5:50 5. The crane that spins in the wind
7:06 6. The giant bearing
8:13 7. The cab at the top
9:19 8. The arm that points up
10:30 9. The crane that unfolds itself
11:34 10. The pins that came out too early
12:42 11. The crane that takes down the crane
13:49 The verdict

Sources:
- Tower crane parts (jib, counter-jib, counterweight, slewing ring, climbing frame, ties, load moment limiters, free slewing/weathervaning): Wikipedia, "Tower crane" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tower_crane ; Liebherr tower crane documentation https://www.liebherr.com/en/int/products/tower-cranes/
- Load charts and limiters, wind limits for operation: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart CC "Cranes and Derricks in Construction" https://www.osha.gov/cranes-derricks ; UK HSE, "Tower cranes" https://www.hse.gov.uk/construction/
- Bellevue, Washington crane collapse (16 November 2006, one death, base design): Washington State L&I report; Wikipedia, "2006 Bellevue crane collapse" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Bellevue_crane_collapse
- Seattle crane collapse (27 April 2019, four deaths, pins removed early during disassembly): Washington State L&I citations; Wikipedia, "2019 Seattle crane collapse" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Seattle_crane_collapse
- Luffing jib cranes and oversailing: Wikipedia, "Luffing jib crane" ; UK oversail licences
- Self-erecting cranes: Potain / Liebherr self-erecting crane product pages
- Dismantling cranes from the top of skyscrapers (derrick cranes, smaller cranes lowered by lift): Wikipedia, "Tower crane" (section on dismantling)
